findings.claim: Q2 distractor A is not a false statement: it is true of every aid in the district AND is entailed by the very observation the stem describes, so a complaining student has a literal argument for it.
findings.evidence: Stem Q2: "What is implied about a buoy that is found some way from the position printed on the chart?" Option A: "Its mooring chain must be longer than the depth of the water it lies in." Passage P2: "A floating aid is fixed to nothing; it is moored, and a mooring has to be slack. Chain longer than the depth lets the buoy lift to a sea instead of being pulled under by it" and "the more chain it has, the wider the ground it can wander over, so the light is somewhere inside that circle rather than on the cross printed on the chart" — i.e. the swing that puts the light off its cross exists BECAUSE the chain exceeds the depth, so displacement entails A. The unit's own rationale concedes the truth of A while calling it a trap: "it restates the surface fact that chain exceeds depth ('thirty-one metres of it for eleven metres of water'), which is true of every aid in the district and therefore answers nothing about the buoy in the stem".
findings.why: Does not flip the key or any verdict: only C discriminates (it excludes the alternative explanation — a dragged sinker — that the stem's observation invites), C is the option that answers the question asked, and both blind solvers returned C (verdicts-vfinal/verdicts-gkey-1 and -2, solver_answer C, 2-0). Recorded because 'a distractor that is actually defensible once you read everything together' is precisely the integrated stage's remit and no review record notes it; the mitigation lives only in the generator's own rationale.

findings.claim: Two internal numbers reconcile only under assumptions the text never states — the 35-metre wander exceeds the geometric maximum for the one buoy whose scope the text gives, and buoy 43's morning runs about four times the stated benchmark turnaround.
findings.evidence: Geometry: P1 "thirty-one metres of it for eleven metres of water"; P5 "it goes back over the side on the scope its master chose" and P4 "Rufus Cadell has had the Marram for thirty-one years and lays his buoys long" — so buoy 43 is a long-laid buoy at 31 m / 11 m, whose maximum horizontal offset with the chain bar-taut is sqrt(31^2 - 11^2) = 28.98 m, and the passage insists the chain is never taut ("a mooring has to be slack"; wear "gathers in the length that sweeps the ground"). Prigent's figure: "the buoys laid longest sit as much as 35 metres from their charted places for hours together." Timeline: "At twenty past six the crane on the Marram takes the weight" vs "By nine o'clock buoy 43 has a scraped skirt, a new lamp and eleven fresh links at the swivel" = ~2 h 40 min, against "In flat water a lift, a scrape, a fresh lamp and a relay take about forty minutes."
findings.why: Neither is a contradiction — other long-laid stations may be deeper (the district holds "two hundred and fourteen floating aids" at unstated depths), and the forty-minute figure is expressly conditioned on "In flat water" and does not include renewing eleven links at the swivel. No key or rationale depends on either number, so the integrated verdict (MINOR_NOTES) is untouched; logged because these are the two arithmetic reconciliations a sharp student can actually run.

findings.claim: The passage recycles both of its spelled-out numbers for unrelated quantities and renders the only other metre figure in digits — a numeral-style wobble a BrE desk would normalise, left standing by a CORRECTED language pass.
findings.evidence: "thirty-one metres of it for eleven metres of water" (P1) vs "Rufus Cadell has had the Marram for thirty-one years" (P4); "eleven metres of water" (P1) vs "eleven fresh links at the swivel" (P5); and "as much as 35 metres from their charted places" (P4) in digits where the other two metre quantities are spelled out. generator_meta claims this as design: "numeric register mixes digits (43, 1911, 1968, 2019, 35), spelled-out numerals (thirty-one, two hundred and fourteen) and a fraction (a fifth)".
findings.why: Cosmetic and arguably deliberate (instrument-measured data in figures, crew rules of thumb spelled out), and no item keys on any of these numbers. Reported because the doubled 'thirty-one' and doubled 'eleven' read as accidental echo rather than register variety, and because it is the residue a native-expert language read owns. The language stage did do real work on this unit — candidates -> candidates-corrected fixes the number-agreement error in Q2/B, "A buoy on the longest moorings" -> "A buoy on the longest mooring" — so CORRECTED stands.

findings.claim: The opening image assigns to the buoy an action the passage's own mechanism paragraph assigns to the chain: a floating buoy does not grind the seabed.
findings.evidence: P1: "On deck it is a tonne of steel that has spent three years grinding a slow arc across the seabed" — antecedent is the buoy, which "comes up out of the Cleyburn approaches" while "The chain comes up after it" as a separate object. P2 then locates ground contact in the chain: "It gathers in the length that sweeps the ground", with the sinker as "the block of iron that holds the whole arrangement to the bottom."
findings.why: Defensible as licensed reportage metonymy (the buoy is the agent that drags the chain that grinds), and the unit never depends on the literal reading: Q1's key correctly attributes ground contact to the chain — "It builds up where the chain drags on the bottom and close to the swivel." Not verdict-changing; noted as the one sentence where the passage's physics and its own later explanation diverge.

findings.claim: generator_meta.length_tell miscounts three of five option lengths and misdescribes the Q3 spread, though the substantive no-length-tell claim survives recount.
findings.evidence: Metadata: "No key is the longest option in its question: Q1 A(18)>B(15); Q2 B(17)>C(15); Q3 A ties at 14-15 with B/D and is not sole longest; Q4 B(17)>D(13); Q5 A(17)>B(14)." Recount (word tokens): Q1 A=17 B=15 C=14 D=14; Q2 A=15 B=17 C=16 D=13; Q3 A=15 B=15 C=14 D=16 (D is the sole longest, not a tie band of 14-15); Q4 A=11 B=17 C=16 D=14; Q5 A=17 B=14 C=14 D=14. Also engineered_traps lists only "wrong_location at Q1/D" while the Q1 rationale tags D twice, "wrong_location / surface_word_match".
findings.why: The claim the metadata exists to support — no key is the longest option in its item — is true on recount for all five questions, and all 20 options sit inside the blueprint's 8-20 word band with no key reusing a >=4-word run from the passage (verified mechanically). Metadata/text cross-consistency is the integrated stage's own remit, so the off-by-ones are logged, but they change nothing student-facing.

findings.claim: All three review records are verdict-only, so no recorded verdict can be falsified from the records themselves; the artifacts, however, substantiate each one.
findings.evidence: reviews/language.jsonl, pedagogy.jsonl, integrated.jsonl each carry a single line for this unit with keys candidate_id/stage/verdict/reviewed_by/date and no findings field. Artifact evidence instead: candidates -> candidates-corrected = the language edit (Q2/B "the longest moorings" -> "the longest mooring"); candidates-corrected -> candidates-final = the pedagogy/integrated edit, which removed an unsupported factual claim from the Q3/D rationale — old: "present crews, who in fact measure their positions far more closely, with loggers running continuously inside the hulls" (the passage never says the loggers run continuously and never rates them above the lightship's bearings) — replaced by "the text sets the lightship's three bearings a watch and the position loggers Prigent fits inside the buoy hulls side by side as two answers to the same uncertainty and rates neither above the other", with engineered_traps updated to add the previously missing "attribution / hedged decoy at Q3/D".
findings.why: This is why the audit is CONFIRMED rather than REFUTED: the stages demonstrably caught a real agreement error and a real unsupported rationale claim. Independent re-verification found nothing they missed that would flip a verdict — every single-quoted span in every rationale resolves verbatim in current option/passage text; all five family labels match elf/families.json (001 detail, 002 inference, 006 purpose/cause, 004 main idea) and the long_passage_5q block budget (2x001, 1x002, 1x006, 1x004 at edge position 5); all 15 distractor trap tags are sanctioned by blueprint-template.md section 3 and each names the mechanism its prose describes; every factual claim in every rationale checks out against the passage; the law_13 name registry claim re-verified by grep across all shipped candidates-final (Cadell, Prigent, Fewtrell, Osian, Naomi, Rufus, Fenella, Moye, Marram, Gaunt, Cleyburn — zero hits elsewhere); and the 'pick the hedged option' heuristic scores exactly 1/5 as the metadata claims (Q2/C hedged and keyed, Q3/D hedged and wrong, no other option in the sheet hedged).
